title: Google reports benchmark results for its experimental Earth AI geospatial agent
key_facts: On 14 Oct 2026 Google Research reported benchmark results and partner testing for the experimental Geospatial Reasoning agent (GRA) in Google Earth AI.
Full GRA with Gemini 3.8 Flash scored 62.7 plus or minus 2.5 on GeoExpertQueries, averaged over three runs; with basic tools it scored 3.3.
GeoExpertQueries measures how closely a system follows expert workflows, not general answer accuracy.
Estimated model inference cost is $0.199 per query with Gemini 3.8 Flash and $0.688 with Gemini 3.1 Pro, excluding Earth Engine and other services.
WHO AFRO used GRA during an Ebola outbreak in the DR Congo to map 48 exposed settlements and over 45,500 people at risk; Google says it took minutes, not weeks.
Expanded access is limited to a group of early users.
quote_evidence: The headline GeoExpertQueries result—62.7 ± 2.5 for full GRA with Gemini 3.8 Flash—measures how closely a system follows expert workflows, not whether its final answers are correct.
Google says expanded access to GRA’s experimental routes is limited to a group of early users.
why_it_matters_hint: An AI agent that plans map and satellite analyses could speed public-health and disaster work, but the scores are Google's own.
notes: Full text read. Company's own benchmark and partner claims. Event 14 Oct, so score lowered.
